impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO contributes to the Apply AI Strategy by deploying validated AI agent systems across three operational sectors. WP5 (NIHS lead) delivers a clinical decision support agent (D5-02) validated on 500 de-identified clinical cases, demonstrating AI adoption in healthcare — one of the Apply AI Strategy's prioritised sectors (IMP-2 expected_impact_alignment). WP6 (ISIA lead) delivers a multi-agent manufacturing process optimisation system (D6-02) demonstrated in an operational pilot factory, driving AI adoption in advanced manufacturing with targets of ≥15% defect reduction and ≥10% energy savings (IMP-3 indicators). WP7 (ELI lead) delivers a logistics and supply chain agent system (D7-02) validated across multi-actor supply chain corridors, extending AI adoption to the logistics sector and providing cross-sector transferability evidence (IMP-4). These three sector-specific demonstrators, each linked to WP deliverables in wp_structure.json, collectively produce a validated evidence base for the Apply AI Strategy goal of advancing AI adoption across European economic sectors.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO advances European open strategic autonomy by producing a European-origin AI agent technology stack that provides an alternative to scale-only approaches from non-European platforms. WP2 (ATU lead) delivers the neuro-symbolic planning engine (D2-02) integrating HTN and MCTS planning with LLM heuristics under formal pre/post-conditions. WP3 (BIIS lead) delivers the adaptive tri-store memory architecture (D3-02) enabling long-horizon agent coherence. WP4 (CERIA lead) delivers formally verified multi-agent coordination protocols (D4-02) with mathematical convergence guarantees — a differentiating capability absent from proprietary platforms (IMP-1 description). The open-source MAESTRO framework (D8-02/WP8; D9-02/WP9) is released under an open licence enabling European researchers and companies to build next-generation AI agent applications without dependency on proprietary non-European AI agent infrastructure (IMP-5 description and indicators), directly instantiating the call destination's open strategic autonomy objective.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO deploys AI agent innovations across European economic sectors through an explicit EDIH-mediated dissemination strategy coordinated by WP9 (BAL lead). The healthcare demonstrator (D5-02/WP5) is disseminated to hospital networks through EDIHs, with NIHS and BAL jointly enabling hospital adoption pathways (IMP-2 exploitation route: EDIH-mediated dissemination to hospitals). The manufacturing demonstrator (D6-02/WP6) is scaled through EIT Manufacturing and the EDIH network, targeting ≥5 European manufacturing SMEs in technology transfer by M48 (IMP-3 indicators). The logistics demonstrator (D7-02/WP7) is disseminated through EDIH channels to logistics and automotive sector actors (IMP-4 exploitation route: EDIH dissemination). The open-source MAESTRO framework (D8-02/WP8; D9-02/WP9) is actively disseminated through ≥3 EDIHs to lower barriers for European SMEs and startups building AI agent applications (IMP-5 indicator: ≥3 EDIHs actively disseminating MAESTRO technology), providing a horizontal platform for AI agent deployment across sectors beyond those directly demonstrated.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO strengthens the European AI research and innovation community through three complementary, explicitly linked channels. First, the MAESTRO benchmark suite (D8-01/WP8) is hosted publicly on the AI-on-demand platform and positioned for adoption as a community evaluation standard (OUT-7 exploitation route), with a target of ≥5 external research groups adopting the benchmark by M48 (IMP-5 indicator). Second, the open-source MAESTRO framework (D8-02/WP8; D9-02/WP9) is contributed to the AI-on-demand platform as a shared infrastructure resource, enabling European researchers and SMEs to build on MAESTRO's planning (D2-02/WP2), memory (D3-02/WP3), and coordination (D4-02/WP4) advances without platform lock-in (IMP-5 description; OUT-8 exploitation route). Third, the coordination protocol specification (D4-01/WP4) underpins ≥1 standardisation proposal to ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 or IEEE (IMP-6 indicator) and is targeted for adoption by ≥3 external multi-agent research projects, directly communicating MAESTRO's scientific advances to the broader European and global research community. Scientific publications (≥20 papers in top venues per IMP-1 indicator) further disseminate the planning, memory, and coordination research outputs.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO builds European technological capacity through the development, validation to TRL 5, and open release of four foundational AI agent technology components: neuro-symbolic planning engine (D2-02/WP2), adaptive tri-store memory architecture (D3-02/WP3), formally verified multi-agent coordination protocols (D4-02/WP4), and the MAESTRO evaluation framework (D8-01/WP8). Each component is validated within the MAESTRO cross-demonstrator evaluation framework (D8-01) and released openly (D9-02/WP9), creating a durable and independently accessible European AI agent technology base. This pathway is mapped to IMP-1 (impacts.json), which explicitly links these deliverables to European AI agent technology capacity advancement. Note: specific AI Factories, Data Labs, or Testing and Experiment Facilities are not named in Tier 3 project data — see coverage_notes for partial coverage flag.
impact_pathways.coverage_notes: Tier 3 project data (impacts.json, outcomes.json) does not explicitly name AI Factories, Data Labs, or Testing and Experiment Facilities as validation infrastructure engaged by the MAESTRO consortium. The pathway is mapped to IMP-1 (impacts.json), which explicitly links D2-02, D3-02, D4-02, D8-01, and D9-02 to European AI agent technology capacity building. The technology capacity-building dimension of EI-05 is addressed through these validated and openly released research outputs, and the three sector demonstrators (WP5, WP6, WP7) validate AI agent results in real operational environments. However, explicit co-location with or use of EU AI Factories, Data Labs, or TEFs infrastructure is not confirmed in any Tier 3 source document. This constitutes partial coverage of EI-05. Full coverage requires a Tier 3 update identifying specific AI Factories or TEFs with which the consortium has established engagement or testing arrangements.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: MAESTRO delivers real-world AI agent impact across the procedurally mandated priority sectors. Healthcare: WP5 (NIHS lead) produces a clinical decision support agent (D5-02/OUT-4) validated on 500 de-identified clinical cases with specialist sub-agents for imaging, laboratory, and guideline reasoning, targeting ≥3 hospital networks in post-project adoption planning by M48 and clinical validation report acceptance by ≥1 national health technology assessment body (IMP-2 indicators). Advanced manufacturing: WP6 (ISIA lead) produces a multi-agent manufacturing process optimisation system (D6-02/OUT-5) demonstrated in a pilot factory environment, targeting ≥15% defect reduction and ≥10% energy savings (IMP-3 indicators). In-vehicle autonomous driving: MAESTRO does not deliver a dedicated autonomous driving demonstrator; however, IMP-4 (impacts.json) explicitly includes 'Architectural transferability mapping to in-vehicle autonomous driving completed' as a project indicator delivered through WP7's cross-sector generalisation work (D7-02/OUT-6), establishing the MAESTRO architecture's applicability to the autonomous driving sector. This combination addresses the call's portfolio coverage requirement across all three procedurally mandated sectors.
impact_pathways.coverage_status: Covered — autonomous driving sector via explicit Inferred linkage in IMP-4
impact_pathways.coverage_notes: Healthcare (WP5/D5-02) and advanced manufacturing (WP6/D6-02) sectors are directly covered by dedicated demonstrators with explicit Tier 3 linkage. In-vehicle autonomous driving coverage is via the IMP-4 indicator 'Architectural transferability mapping to in-vehicle autonomous driving completed' (impacts.json IMP-4.indicators), explicitly stated in Tier 3 but not supported by a dedicated demonstrator work package. Per CLAUDE.md §12.2, the autonomous driving dimension is classified as Inferred: the inference chain is IMP-4.indicators (explicit Tier 3) → WP7 cross-sector generalisation activity (T7-03) → D7-02 (explicit linked_deliverable_ids). This inference is stated and the source documented.

dissemination_plan.open_access_policy: All peer-reviewed publications produced within MAESTRO shall be made available as Open Access in conformance with Horizon Europe mandatory open access requirements (General Annex L). Immediate Gold Open Access is the primary route; where publisher agreements require it, Green Open Access deposit in an institutional or discipline-specific repository with the maximum permitted embargo is the compliant secondary route. All software outputs — including the neuro-symbolic planning engine (D2-02/WP2), adaptive memory architecture (D3-02/WP3), coordination protocol implementation (D4-02/WP4), MAESTRO evaluation framework and benchmark suite (D8-01, D8-02/WP8), and the community platform (D9-02/WP9) — are released under open licences (Apache 2.0 or equivalent) via the AI-on-demand platform and GitHub. Research datasets generated during healthcare (WP5/NIHS), manufacturing (WP6/ISIA), and logistics (WP7/ELI) demonstrator validation activities are governed by the project Data Management Plan (DMP, M6) and made FAIR-compliant and publicly accessible where clinical data protection obligations, ethics approvals, and applicable data protection law (GDPR) permit.

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: MAESTRO adopts a differentiated IPR strategy aligned with the project's dual mandate of European open strategic autonomy and sector-specific commercial exploitation. Core foundational research outputs — the neuro-symbolic planning engine (WP2/ATU), adaptive tri-store memory architecture (WP3/BIIS), formally verified multi-agent coordination protocol suite (WP4/CERIA), and the MAESTRO evaluation framework and benchmark suite (WP8) — are released under open licences (Apache 2.0 or equivalent) to maximise European ecosystem accessibility, AI-on-demand platform integration, and independence from non-European proprietary AI agent platforms, as required by IMP-5. Any patentable innovations arising from the coordination protocol formal verification work (WP4/CERIA) are assessed for patent protection prior to public disclosure to support the standardisation submission strategy and preserve freedom to operate. Sector-specific demonstrator outputs (healthcare D5-02/NIHS, manufacturing D6-02/ISIA, logistics D7-02/ELI) are governed by a Joint Technology Transfer Agreement negotiated in WP9 (BAL lead) and concluded before M12, with NIHS, ISIA, and ELI retaining primary exploitation rights in their respective application domains consistent with their operational integration commitments. All IPR arrangements comply with Horizon Europe IP provisions in the Model Grant Agreement.

sustainability_mechanism.description: MAESTRO's post-project sustainability is assured through four complementary mechanisms grounded in explicit partner commitments and the project's open-ecosystem design. First, the open-source MAESTRO framework (D8-02/WP8) and evaluation benchmark suite (D8-01/WP8) are contributed to the AI-on-demand platform under long-term maintenance commitments coordinated by BAL (WP9 lead), with community governance transferred to an open-source stewardship model by M48 — ensuring independent, multi-actor maintenance beyond the grant period without dependency on continued project funding. Second, each sector-specific demonstrator is operationally embedded by its lead partner: NIHS integrates the clinical decision support agent into its clinical informatics infrastructure for continued operation post-M60; ISIA embeds the manufacturing multi-agent system in the pilot factory production environment with an operational continuity plan completed by M48; and ELI integrates the logistics agent into its live supply chain operational systems under the ELI integration roadmap (M48). Third, EDIH network activation — targeting ≥3 EDIHs actively disseminating MAESTRO technology by M48 (IMP-5 indicator; KPI-05) — ensures that MAESTRO innovations continue to reach European economic actors through EDIH operational infrastructure, staff, and budgets that persist beyond the project period. Fourth, CERIA's standardisation engagement in ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 or IEEE (WP4) positions MAESTRO coordination protocol results as inputs to international standards processes, which sustain the technical contributions through the full standards lifecycle independently of project continuation.
